bugs.name: CSV append and replacement notifications link to /model/undefined
bugs.summary: Successful append and replace uploads to an existing model produce a broken filename link. Clicking it opens a blank new question. Reproduced twice with append and once with replacement; the data operations succeed.
bugs.expected: The success notification's filename link opens the existing model receiving the uploaded data.
bugs.actual: Both append and replace notifications link to /model/undefined. Clicking redirects to a blank New question with no starting data, although row changes persist.
reproSteps: Sign in as administrator. In Admin settings → Uploads, enable uploads using Sample Database and PUBLIC schema.
Open a personal collection and upload AD Upload.csv with columns name,amount,date and rows Alpha,10,2026-10-01; Beta,20,2026-10-02; Gamma,30,2026-10-03.

Choose Upload data to this model → Append data to this model and upload AD Append.csv with the same columns and row Delta,40,2026-10-04.
Click AD Append.csv in the successful 'Data added to' notification. The link targets /model/undefined and opens an empty new question.

reproSteps: Sign in as a user who can create metrics and open /browse/metrics.
Create a new metric with the plus button and leave the Data picker empty.
Click Save, enter a fresh unique name, and choose a collection where the user can save metrics.
Submit the save dialog and observe the DATABASE_ID constraint error and SQL INSERT statement instead of guidance to select starting data.

bugs.name: Failed CSV replacement deletes existing model data
bugs.summary: Replacing an uploaded model with a CSV containing an invalid numeric or date value reports a validation error but deletes all existing rows. Reproduced repeatedly from valid populated states. Missing-column replacement and invalid append preserved data, isolating this failure to replacement value parsing.
bugs.expected: An invalid replacement is rejected and leaves the existing model data unchanged.
bugs.actual: The upload reports "'notanumber' is not a recognizable number" (or an invalid-date parsing error). After reloading, the model shows 'No results!' and 0 rows; its original data is lost.
reproSteps: As administrator, enable uploads in Admin settings → Uploads using Sample Database and PUBLIC schema.
Upload AD Upload.csv in a collection with columns name,amount,date and rows Alpha,10,2026-10-01; Beta,20,2026-10-02; Gamma,30,2026-10-03.
Open the created model and verify its existing rows.
Choose Upload data to this model → Replace all data in this model. Upload AD Invalid Replacement.csv with the same columns and row Invalid,notanumber,2026-10-08.
Observe the Upload error and numeric parsing error. Close the dialog and reload the model.
Observe 'No results!' and 'Showing 0 rows', rather than the original rows. A replacement containing a valid row followed by an invalid date also produces the same data loss.

bugs.expected: Refreshing the record URL should reopen the same record details.
bugs.actual: After refresh, the app opens the model's Query/Columns/Settings editor, with Cancel and Save changes, instead of the record. Verified on a saved model with record_key='query': before refresh its dialog displayed 'QA Query Key' and 'record_key query'; after refresh the same /model/<id>-<slug>/query URL displayed the SQL model editor.
reproSteps: Open /browse/models → Create a new model → Use a native query, using the Release operations database.
Run SELECT 'query' AS record_key, 'QA Query Key' AS title and save it as 'QA Reserved Key Model'.
Choose the model's three-dot menu → Edit metadata → Columns. Set record_key's Column type to Entity Key, and title's Column type to Entity Name.
In the model editor's Settings tab, select List and Save changes.
Click QA Query Key in the model list. Confirm its record details appear and the browser URL ends with /model/<model-id>-qa-reserved-key-model/query.
Refresh the browser at that URL.

bugs.name: Opening a model record with numeric entity key 0 leaves the URL at the model list
bugs.summary: Opening a model record with numeric entity key 0 leaves the URL at the model list.
bugs.expected: The zero record should have its own URL ending in /0, and refreshing should preserve the selected record, as it does for other keys.
bugs.actual: QA Zero Record opens with record_key 0, but the URL remains /model/<id>-<slug>. Next row changes the URL to /model/<id>-<slug>/-1, and Previous row returns to the bare model URL while displaying key 0. Refresh closes the record and loads the list. The full-page control correctly exposes /model/<id>-<slug>/detail/0, demonstrating that 0 is a valid record key. Repeated through direct list clicks and next/previous navigation.
reproSteps: Open /browse/models → Create a new model → Use a native query, using Release operations.
Run SELECT 0 AS record_key, 'QA Zero Record' AS title UNION ALL SELECT -1 AS record_key, 'QA Negative Record' AS title and save as 'QA Zero Key Model'.
Open the model's three-dot menu → Edit metadata → Columns. Set record_key to Entity Key and title to Entity Name.
In the editor's Settings tab, select List and Save changes.
Click QA Zero Record and inspect the address bar. Click Next row, then Previous row, and compare the URLs.
Refresh while QA Zero Record is open.

bugs.name: Records from a trashed model remain in normal search results
bugs.summary: Records from a trashed model remain in normal search results.
bugs.expected: Normal search should exclude records belonging to trashed models. They should only appear when searching trash, if supported.
bugs.actual: After enabling Title record search on a Products model and trashing that model, searching Rustic Paper Wallet still returns its indexed record. This persists after full page reload with Search items in trash unchecked.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai and open /browse/models → Create a new model.
Choose the query builder and Sample Database → Products. Run the model and save it with a unique name such as QA Searchable Products.
On the saved model, open the three-dot menu → Edit metadata, then Columns. Select the Title column by clicking its name.
Turn on “Surface individual records in search by matching against this column” and Save changes.
Use global Search for Rustic Paper Wallet; wait until a record in the new model appears, confirming indexing is ready.
Return to the model and use its three-dot menu → Move to trash, then confirm.
Search Rustic Paper Wallet again and open View and filter all results. Keep Search items in trash off, and reload the search page.
Observe that the record still appears. Open it to see the model's trash banner.

bugs.name: Searching models and metrics by date uses the server's GMT day, so recent items fall on the wrong day
bugs.summary: Search's Creation date and Last edit date filters for models and metrics resolve dates on the server's GMT clock, so items created or edited in the evening in a timezone behind UTC are filtered as the next day.
bugs.expected: A date filter on the search page includes an item edited or created minutes ago under Today, and Before/On a date matches the day the user sees.
bugs.actual: After 00:00 GMT (for example after 5 PM in PT), an item edited minutes earlier disappears from Last edit: Today, and items created that local day disappear from Creation date: Before tomorrow.
reproSteps: Do this in a timezone behind UTC, after 00:00 GMT (for example after 5 PM Pacific).
Create a metric with a unique name (for example by duplicating Number of Orders), then make and save an edit to it.
Search its unique name, open View and filter all results, and select content type Metric.
Set Creation date to Fixed date range > On today's date as shown in the picker; the metric appears.
Open Last edit date, select Current then Day. Observe no results instead of the metric edited minutes ago.

bugs.name: Saving model metadata adds hidden FK display columns, so the Info panel field count goes up
bugs.summary: Saving model metadata adds hidden FK display columns, so the Info panel field count goes up.
bugs.expected: Editing one column's display name should leave the model's columns unchanged. The Info panel should keep showing '9 fields' (ID, User ID, Product ID, Subtotal, Tax, Total, Discount, Created At, Quantity).
bugs.actual: After saving, the Info panel shows '11 fields', which now include 'User → User ID' and 'Product → Product ID'. GET /api/card/:id result_metadata now has 11 entries, the extra ones being NAME (display 'User ID') and TITLE (display 'Product ID'). The table view still shows only 9 columns. The same thing happened to the example model 'Orders + People', which went from 12 to 14 fields.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai
Create a model on Sample Database > Orders (no joins or changes). Its Info > Overview shows '9 fields'
Open the model's ... menu > Edit metadata (Columns tab)
Click the Subtotal column and change Display name to 'Subtotal X', then click Save changes
Open the Info (i) panel > Overview
It now says '11 fields' and lists 'User → User ID' and 'Product → Product ID'

bugs.name: Model basic Update action silently sets untouched boolean fields to false
bugs.summary: Model basic Update action silently sets untouched boolean fields to false.
bugs.expected: Only the fields the user edits are updated; untouched optional fields (including booleans) keep their existing values.
bugs.actual: Invoice ID 2 had EXPECTED_INVOICE = true. After running Update with only ID=2 and Plan='QAPlan2', the row became EXPECTED_INVOICE = false. Request body: {"parameters":{"date_received":null,"plan":"QAPlan2","expected_invoice":false,"payment":null,"account_id":null,"id":2}}. Rows 1 and 2 now show false while every other invoice shows true.
reproSteps: Make sure actions are enabled for Sample Database
Create a model on the Invoices table (e.g. 'QA Products Model'), open /model/<id>/detail/actions and click 'Create basic actions'
Check invoice ID 2: Expected Invoice = true
From the model's Actions, run Update with ID 2 and Plan QAPlan2, leaving Expected Invoice untouched.
Open the model's data: invoice 2 now shows Expected Invoice = false
